column1: # Stream npcanim2 (TOP50 round 5): per-creature ATTACK and BLOCK animations for creatures that
# carry NO weapon-family parameter 2816 - the ones round 4's table cannot reach, including the
# Varrock guards and the elemental wizards the user reported still standing rigid.
# THE ROUTE. A creature that wields a weapon is DRAWN HOLDING IT. Its 950 definition's `models`
# array contains the very worn model an item definition publishes in maleEquip1/femaleEquip1/
# maleEquip2/femaleEquip2, so the model maps back to the items that wear it, their own parameter
# 686 names the weapon struct, and that struct's parameter 2914 (typed ANIMATION by the cache's own
# ParamType table) is the attack sequence, 2917 the block sequence - the same two struct fields
# Native950MeleeWeapons.java:69-70 already reads for a PLAYER holding that weapon. A row ships only
# when the creature's models reach EXACTLY ONE weapon family; two families is a refusal.
# CALIBRATION, not assumption. On the 250 attackable definitions that carry BOTH parameter 2816 and
# a drawn weapon model, 39 are ambiguous and of the remaining 211 the drawn weapon's 2914 equals the
# declared family's 2914 on 183 (86.7%). The 28 disagreements are all the same shape - the creature
# is drawn with a specific named weapon of a neighbouring melee family (Elite Sotapanna 25574
# declares 14930 and is drawn with a Tetsu katana, struct 14923) - never an unrelated sequence.
# Where both routes exist and disagree the DECLARED family wins and nothing is shipped from the
# model. reports/r5-npcanim2-model-calibration.tsv has all 250.
# RENDER GATE. Native950NpcCombatAnimations.compatibleWithRender refuses a legacy-frame combat
# sequence on a creature whose BAS stand animation is a modern/animaya one. The catalogue applies it
# to the inherited authored animation; the round-4 published table bypasses it. Every row here is
# re-checked against it at startup: an incompatible ATTACK sequence is a hard startup failure (no
# such row is shipped) and an incompatible BLOCK sequence is dropped per creature at runtime, which
# is why Seren archer 22470, Seren warrior 22471, Ancient warrior 22498 and Black Knights
# 22488/22489 will swing but not flinch. Seren mage 22472 and Necromancer 22478 are REFUSED
# outright by that gate: their only candidate, staff 18321, is legacy and their stand 37633 is not.
# EVIDENCE CLASSES, stated per row and asserted at startup:
#   A - the RS3 wiki names the weapon (or its class) on the creature's OWN page, and the cache's
#       drawn model is a weapon of exactly that class. The round-4 bar.
#   B - the creature's own parameter 2816 AND its drawn model independently name the SAME weapon
#       struct: two cache tables agreeing (index 18 parameters vs index 18 models -> index 19 item
#       -> index 22 struct).
#   C - the drawn model alone. The wiki page confirms the creature's id, level and combat style -
#       quoted in the row - but does NOT name its weapon. This is one notch below A and B and is
#       recorded as such: what a class C row plays is the attack of the weapon the client itself
#       draws in that creature's hand, so a wrong row is a swing of a neighbouring melee family,
#       never an unrelated sequence. 86.7% is the measured agreement rate above.
# Everything the row depends on - the creature (index 18), the carrier item (index 19), the struct
# (index 22) and both sequences (index 20) - is SHA-256 pinned in npcanim2-950.properties and
# re-read at startup by Native950NpcDrawnWeapons.verifyCacheBindings().
